about.title: About
about.description: Physicist turned AI engineer — building systems that think and compute.
paragraphs: I'm Brian, a researcher working where semiconductor physics meets AI systems. During my master's I used first-principles calculations (DFT) to study the electronic properties of ZnO and heterostructures, and published 3 SCI journal papers on band engineering and catalytic reactions.

I also build AI agent systems hands-on — self-hosted LLM services, RAG knowledge bases, and a personal AI work system. I believe a good engineer doesn't just solve problems; they build systems that keep evolving.

categories.name: Computational Materials
categories.intro: Used first-principles calculations during my master's to study oxide electronic structure and catalytic reactions; the results went into 3 SCI journal papers.

tags.name: VASP
tags.detail: Primary calculation engine. Used for structure relaxation and electronic structure of ZnO thin films and metal-nanoparticle / oxide interfaces.

tags.name: DFT
tags.detail: The core method: band structures, adsorption, and reaction pathways. Also paired with DFT-1/2 to correct the bandgap underestimation of ZnO.

tags.name: Quantum ESPRESSO
tags.detail: Standalone plane-wave DFT tool used as a cross-check, following the same workflow as VASP (structure, band structure, DOS).

tags.name: Band Structure
tags.detail: Used to explain ZnO thin-film bandgaps and Type-II band alignment in heterostructures, connecting bandgap prediction to photocatalytic charge separation.

tags.name: DOS
tags.detail: Used to inspect electronic state distributions of surfaces and adsorbate systems, helping identify charge transfer and active sites.

tags.name: NEB
tags.detail: Used to estimate transition states and energy barriers of surface reactions (such as the HER pathway), extending adsorption energies into reaction kinetics.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Aided DFT-1/2 Calculations for Bandgaps of Zinc Oxide Thin Films
papers.description: Combined the DFT-1/2 method with genetic-algorithm artificial neural networks (GANNs) to predict ZnO thin-film bandgaps. GANN predictions differ from the DFT-1/2 values by less than 5% and match experimental data closely.

papers.title: Catalytic Hydrogen Evolution Reaction on Surfaces of Metal-Nanoparticle-Coated Zinc-Based Oxides by First-Principles Calculations
papers.journal: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, 2022 — IF: 7.2
papers.description: Used first-principles calculations to study the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalysed by Pt/Au/Ag nanoparticle-coated ZnO surfaces. Au/ZnO showed adsorption free energy closest to zero, while Pt/ZnO performed best along the Volmer–Heyrovsky pathway.

papers.title: Mg₂Fe₂O₅ Nanoparticle-Decorated Ca₂Fe₂O₅−CaFe₂O₄ Heterostructure for Efficient Photocatalytic CO₂ Conversion
papers.description: The study paired a Mg₂Fe₂O₅-decorated Ca₂Fe₂O₅−CaFe₂O₄ heterostructure with DFT calculations for photocatalytic CO₂ reduction. The calculations revealed a Type-II charge-transfer mechanism and accounted for the 81.7% CH₄ selectivity.
